text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Thursday:
- Some 10 regional newspapers based in South-East Switzerland announced plans to appear under one single titel. Die Suedostschweiz will rank as the country's eight largest paper.
- Swiss textile and building equipment maker Zellweger-Luwa registered a 4.5 percent increase in sales to 1.06 billion Swiss francs in 1996. Net profit stagnated at 27.2 million francs.
- Bankrupt financier Werner Ray may soon be returned to Switzerland as a Bahama high court rejected Rays appeal against an lower court's extradition ruling.
- Swiss National Bank shares registered a hefty boost on Wednesday with shares trading at 1,100 francs, up 33 percent compared to the previous day.

- Swiss economy minister Jean-Pascal Delamuraz addressed the issue of the so-called Marcos dollars during his official visit to the Philipines. Some $500 million of the former ruler are still locked in Swiss bank acounts.
- Swiss watch producer TAG Heuer reported a 1996 net profit of 60.5 million Swiss francs, up 15.7 percent compared to the previous year. Sales rose by 10.6 percent to 419.7 million francs.
